abstract: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense tropical race 4 (Foc TR4) poses a major threat to global banana production, yet quantitative variation in resistance across Musa diversity remains poorly characterised. In this study, 21 accessions representing many of the major cultivated Musa groups and wild relatives were evaluated for their response to Foc TR4 under controlled-environment conditions. Significant variation in Foc TR4-associated corm discolouration was observed across the panel. Eight accessions had significantly less corm discolouration than the susceptible control Dwarf Cavendish: five were classified as resistant (all plants with more than 80% healthy corm area): Musa itinerans, M. schizocarpa, FHIA-02, FHIA-21 and the plantain Curare, and three as tolerant, which response was significantly different to the Dwarf Cavendish control but with some plants affected: M. ornata, Pelipita and Mai'a Maoli Koa'e. All accessions with only A genomes were susceptible or very susceptible, as were M. textilis and the B-containing triploids Pome (AAB) and Silver Bluggoe (ABB). Five of the seven accessions carrying at least one B genome were resistant or tolerant, suggesting that B-genome backgrounds merit wider screening as potential sources of resistance. These results identify valuable sources of resistance to Foc TR4 and provide a basis for banana breeding and further investigation of the genetic basis of resistance at the cultivar level.
